replies.reason: elif tests a further condition and else runs when no earlier branch matched; checked on Python 3.13.
list.append, list.remove and list.sort mutate in place and return None; checked on Python 3.13.
replies.assert:
x = [3, 1, 2]
assert x.append(4) is None and x == [3, 1, 2, 4]
assert x.remove(3) is None and x == [1, 2, 4]
assert x.sort() is None and x == [1, 2, 4]
y = [2, 1]
assert y.sort() is None and y == [1, 2]

replies.reason: super() gives access to the parent's method so the child can extend it; checked on Python 3.13. With multiple inheritance it follows the method resolution order, a detail beginners can skip.
In Python 3 map and filter return lazy iterators, so list() is needed to see results. 'The same way' depends on the previous lesson, which is not shown.
replies.assert:
m = map(str, [1, 2])
f = filter(None, [0, 1])
assert not isinstance(m, list) and not isinstance(f, list)
assert iter(m) is m and iter(f) is f
assert list(m) == ["1", "2"] and list(f) == [1]
assert list(m) == []
